parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Find the probability that more than 9 of these students play at least one musical instrument. 
A random sample of 90 students from the college is now chosen.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Use an approximation to find the probability that fewer than 40 of these students play exactly
one musical instrument.

text: In a large college, 28% of the students do not play any musical instrument, 52% play exactly one
musical instrument and the remainder play two or more musical instruments.
A random sample of 12 students from the college is chosen.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the number of different arrangements of the 9 letters in the word CROCODILE.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the number of different arrangements of the 9 letters in the word CROCODILE in which
there is a C at each end and the two Os are not together.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Four letters are selected from the 9 letters in the word CROCODILE.
Find the number of selections in which the number of Cs is not the same as the number of Os.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Find the number of ways in which the 9 letters in the word CROCODILE can be divided into
three groups, each containing three letters, if the two Cs must be in different groups.

parts.text: Find the probability that all 3 eggs chosen contain the same colour sweet.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Find the probability that all 3 eggs chosen contain a yellow sweet, given that all three children
have the same colour sweet.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Find the probability that at least one of Hanna’s three children chooses an egg that contains an
orange sweet.
